name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.
    #
    # Enforcement path (review thread 1): a `needs:`-dependent job whose
    # dependency fails reports `skipped`, and skipped counts as a
    # SUCCESSFUL status for required checks. Today quality.yml is
    # dispatch-only (the SM tick stamps required contexts from the run
    # outcome), but this job must also go RED on its own: `if: always()`
    # + the result guard below keep the shape safe if a `pull_request`
    # trigger is ever added.
    needs: [static, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail unless static and test both succeeded
        if: needs.static.result != 'success' || needs.test.result != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "static result: ${{ needs.static.result }}; test result: ${{ needs.test.result }}" >&2
          exit 1
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == …

# gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.
    #
    # Enforcement path (review thread 1): a `needs:`-dependent job whose
    # dependency fails reports `skipped`, and skipped counts as a
    # SUCCESSFUL status for required checks. Today quality.yml is
    # dispatch-only (the SM tick stamps required contexts from the run
    # outcome), but this job must also go RED on its own: `if: always()`
    # + the result guard below keep the shape safe if a `pull_request`
    # trigger is ever added.
    needs: [static, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail unless static and test both succeeded
        if: needs.static.result != 'success' || needs.test.result != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "static result: ${{ needs.static.result }}; test result: ${{ needs.test.result }}" >&2
          exit 1
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == …

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt

name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.
    #
    # Enforcement path (review thread 1): a `needs:`-dependent job whose
    # dependency fails reports `skipped`, and skipped counts as a
    # SUCCESSFUL status for required checks. Today quality.yml is
    # dispatch-only (the SM tick stamps required contexts from the run
    # outcome), but this job must also go RED on its own: `if: always()`
    # + the result guard below keep the shape safe if a `pull_request`
    # trigger is ever added.
    needs: [static, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail unless static and test both succeeded
        if: needs.static.result != 'success' || needs.test.result != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "static result: ${{ needs.static.result }}; test result: ${{ needs.test.result }}" >&2
          exit 1
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == …

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.
    #
    # Enforcement path (review thread 1): a `needs:`-dependent job whose
    # dependency fails reports `skipped`, and skipped counts as a
    # SUCCESSFUL status for required checks. Today quality.yml is
    # dispatch-only (the SM tick stamps required contexts from the run
    # outcome), but this job must also go RED on its own: `if: always()`
    # + the result guard below keep the shape safe if a `pull_request`
    # trigger is ever added.
    needs: [static, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail unless static and test both succeeded
        if: needs.static.result != 'success' || needs.test.result != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "static result: ${{ needs.static.result }}; test result: ${{ needs.test.result }}" >&2
          exit 1
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == …

blocks.text:
Interesting! In the sharded run, the actual path contains `scope[]=success` unencoded. In the isolated run it passes. Why would the query encoding differ depending on shard/ordering?

Look at `_listProjectJobs`:

```dart
final query = <String>[
  'per_page=${_clampPerPage(_perPageArg(args))}',
  'page=${_parsePositiveInt(syncAsStr(args['page']), 1)}',
  for (final scope in _scopeList(args['scope']))
    'scope[]=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}',
];
final body = syncBodyOrError(SyncHttpClient.get(
  '${config.baseUrl}/$path?${query.join('&')}',
  headers: config.headers,
));
```

The code encodes scope with Uri.encodeQueryComponent — 'success' has no special chars, so `scope[]=success` would remain... wait, `Uri.encodeQueryComponent('success')` = 'success'. blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.
    #
    # Enforcement path (review thread 1): a `needs:`-dependent job whose
    # dependency fails reports `skipped`, and skipped counts as a
    # SUCCESSFUL status for required checks. Today quality.yml is
    # dispatch-only (the SM tick stamps required contexts from the run
    # outcome), but this job must also go RED on its own: `if: always()`
    # + the result guard below keep the shape safe if a `pull_request`
    # trigger is ever added.
    needs: [static, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail unless static and test both succeeded
        if: needs.static.result != 'success' || needs.test.result != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "static result: ${{ needs.static.result }}; test result: ${{ needs.test.result }}" >&2
          exit 1
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == …

blocks.text:
Interesting! In the sharded run, the actual path contains `scope[]=success` unencoded. In the isolated run it passes. Why would the query encoding differ depending on shard/ordering?

Look at `_listProjectJobs`:

```dart
final query = <String>[
  'per_page=${_clampPerPage(_perPageArg(args))}',
  'page=${_parsePositiveInt(syncAsStr(args['page']), 1)}',
  for (final scope in _scopeList(args['scope']))
    'scope[]=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}',
];
final body = syncBodyOrError(SyncHttpClient.get(
  '${config.baseUrl}/$path?${query.join('&')}',
  headers: config.headers,
));
```

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.
    #
    # Enforcement path (review thread 1): a `needs:`-dependent job whose
    # dependency fails reports `skipped`, and skipped counts as a
    # SUCCESSFUL status for required checks. Today quality.yml is
    # dispatch-only (the SM tick stamps required contexts from the run
    # outcome), but this job must also go RED on its own: `if: always()`
    # + the result guard below keep the shape safe if a `pull_request`
    # trigger is ever added.
    needs: [static, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail unless static and test both succeeded
        if: needs.static.result != 'success' || needs.test.result != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "static result: ${{ needs.static.result }}; test result: ${{ needs.test.result }}" >&2
          exit 1
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == …

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.
    #
    # Enforcement path (review thread 1): a `needs:`-dependent job whose
    # dependency fails reports `skipped`, and skipped counts as a
    # SUCCESSFUL status for required checks. Today quality.yml is
    # dispatch-only (the SM tick stamps required contexts from the run
    # outcome), but this job must also go RED on its own: `if: always()`
    # + the result guard below keep the shape safe if a `pull_request`
    # trigger is ever added.
    needs: [static, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail unless static and test both succeeded
        if: needs.static.result != 'success' || needs.test.result != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "static result: ${{ needs.static.result }}; test result: ${{ needs.test.result }}" >&2
          exit 1
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == 'success'
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        if: needs.static.result == 'success' && needs.test.result == …

```dart
final query = <String>[

final body = syncBodyOrError(SyncHttpClient.get(

));
```

The code encodes scope with Uri.encodeQueryComponent — 'success' has no special chars, so `scope[]=success` would remain... wait, `Uri.encodeQueryComponent('success')` = 'success'. And '[]' are NOT encoded since they're written literally. So the query is `scope[]=success` — the brackets are literal!

But the test expects `scope%5B%5D=success` (encoded brackets). And it passed in isolation?? That's weird. Unless... the echo server decodes/re-encodes the path? The echo server probably reads `self.path` raw. Hmm, but in the isolated run the request was `scope%5B%5D=success`?

Wait — maybe the difference: SyncHttpClient.get uses curl. curl would send the URL as given. Unless curl itself encodes brackets. curl does NOT encode `[]` in URLs by default (it treats them as valid). Hmm.

Actually, wait. Maybe SyncHttpClient sometimes uses a different transport. Or the difference is GitLab config: `config.baseUrl`. In the failing case the request was logged with literal `scope[]`. In the passing case with encoded. Same code path... unless `Uri.encodeQueryComponent` behaves differently? No.

So the bridge does `Uri.parse(url)` then `openUrl(method, uri)`. RFC 3986: query = *( pchar / "/" / "?" ), pchar excludes [ ]. Dart's Uri.parse is forgiving and percent-decodes/keeps... Actually Dart Uri.parse normalizes invalid characters by percent-encoding them? No — Uri.parse keeps characters that aren't valid by encoding? Let me recall: `Uri.parse("http://a/?q=[]")` → the query becomes `%5B%5D`? I believe Dart's Uri parser percent-encodes characters not allowed in the query component. Yes! Dart's Uri implementation encodes disallowed characters (with some exceptions like `[` `]`? no...). Let me verify quickly with dart.

So: bridge transport → `%5B%5D` encoded → matches test expectation. curl transport → literal `[]` (curl sends raw; globbing with empty brackets... maybe passes through) → test fails.

Now, why would the bridge not be ready during the scope test in the sharded run but ready in the isolated run? Timing of `Isolate.spawn` + handshake. `Isolate.spawn` of a new isolate requires... the spawn itself is async — under heavy parallel test load (dart test runs files concurrently), spawning may be delayed. In the isolated run, fewer isolates, spawn completes fast.

But wait — within the file, the first two tests each do `await requestLog()`, which yields multiple event-loop turns. The boot handshake: `Isolate.spawn` → worker starts → sends port via ReceivePort. This needs the VM to schedule the new isolate; typically completes within milliseconds. Under load (CI, 4 shards × concurrency), spawn may take longer... plausibly a few hundred ms. Now, why would the bridge not be ready during the scope test in the sharded run but ready in the isolated run? Timing of `Isolate.spawn` + handshake. `Isolate.spawn` of a new isolate requires... the spawn itself is async — under heavy parallel test load (dart test runs files concurrently), spawning may be delayed. In the isolated run, fewer isolates, spawn completes fast.

But wait — within the file, the first two tests each do `await requestLog()`, which yields multiple event-loop turns. The boot handshake: `Isolate.spawn` → worker starts → sends port via ReceivePort. This needs the VM to schedule the new isolate; typically completes within milliseconds. Under load (CI, 4 shards × concurrency), spawn may take longer... plausibly a few hundred ms. Between test 1 and test 3 there are awaits (HTTP requests to local server — fast, sub-ms). So maybe only a couple of event loop turns between the boot kick (first request in test 1) and test 3's requests. If spawn takes >~10ms under load, still not ready → curl → literal brackets → fail.

Actually, hmm: in test 1, the sync handler runs FIRST (bridge not ready → curl + kick boot), then `await requestLog()` — that's the echo server HTTP request, one round trip ~1ms. Then test 2 same. Then test 3 makes 3 sync requests — likely still curl if spawn is slow.

But in my isolated run, the scope test PASSED — meaning bridge became ready quickly. Race confirmed: **flaky test depending on bridge boot timing**.

The real fix per the ticket: the test must be deterministic. Options:

1. In the test's setUp, ensure deterministic transport. E.g., await the bridge boot explicitly before running (kick boot and await it), or dispose the bridge so curl fallback is used consistently, and make the curl path deterministic by encoding brackets in code: `scope%5B%5D=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}` in `_listProjectJobs` — then both transports send the same bytes. That fixes the production inconsistency too (transport-dependent wire format is a real bug — server may interpret literal `[]` fine, GitLab accepts scope[] either way, but byte-identical requests across transports is the right invariant).

Wait, does GitLab accept `scope%5B%5D=success`? Yes — percent-decoding happens server-side; that's the standard encoding.

But hold on — the test passed in the earlier full-ish run (`dart test/js/sync_tools/ ...` → 680 passed) where many files ran concurrently... and failed in the shard run. Truly load-dependent. Also CI failed at "test (1)" — shard 1.

2. Alternatively make the test tolerant of both encodings: `contains('scope%5B%5D=success')` OR `contains('scope[]=success')`. That papers over the transport race.

Which is correct per project conventions? The deeper bug: **the two transports produce different wire bytes for the same URL**. arguments.content:
# gh-380 rework — fix CI red head on PR #381

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red CI head (`9c452441`)** — a transport-parity flake in
  the new `gitlab_list_project_jobs` tool, reproduced locally against the exact
  CI shard (`dart test --total-shards 4 --shard-index 1`):

  ```text
  ❌ gitlab_list_project_jobs maps scope to repeated scope[] params
  Expected: contains 'scope%5B%5D=success'
  Actual:   '/api/v4/projects/g%2Fr/jobs?per_page=20&page=1&scope[]=success'
  ```

  `SyncHttpClient` has two transports with **different wire behavior for
  non-ASCII URL bytes**: the curl fallback sends the URL string verbatim
  (literal `scope[]=`), while the pooled-isolate bridge routes it through
  `Uri.parse`/`HttpClient`, which percent-encodes to `scope%5B%5D=`. The tool
  built the query with literal brackets and relied on the bridge to encode
  them; whether the bridge or curl serves a request is a `SyncHttpBridge`
  boot-timing race that flips with machine load — green in isolated runs,
  red under the full sharded suite. Verified empirically against a local
  echo server: curl logs `scope[]=success`, Dart `HttpClient` logs
  `scope%5B%5D=success` for the same URL.
- The other red checks (`gate`, `agents-gate`) are downstream merge jobs of
  the failed shards; `static` (format+analyze) passes locally on this head
  and its CI log was not included in the input, so no in-tree cause was
  found — the flake fix plus a fresh head re-arms validation.
- No open PR review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `{"threads": []}`);
  review decision `NONE`.

## Approach

TDD, one finding:

1. **RED** — added a deterministic regression test
   (`scope[] params are wire-identical on both HTTP transports`) that forces
   each transport in turn — `SyncHttpBridge.shared.dispose()` before the sync
   call guarantees the curl fallback, `await SyncHttpBridge.shared.boot()`
   guarantees the isolate bridge — and pins the echo-server-logged path to
   the percent-encoded form on both. Failed pre-fix with the literal
   `scope[]=` wire bytes (the exact CI failure).
2. **GREEN** — `_listProjectJobs` now pre-encodes the param name:
   `scope%5B%5D=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}`. Both transports emit
   identical bytes (`Uri.parse` keeps valid escapes, no double-encoding —
   the pre-existing `%2F` project path confirms). GitLab decodes
   `scope%5B%5D` identically to `scope[]`.
3. **REFACTOR** — moved the new test into its own `testjoblisttools_p5()`
   group: placing it in `p2` pushed that function to 71 lines and failed the
   `method_size` gate (max 60), the same reason the file was originally
   split p1–p4. Doc comment on `_listProjectJobs` now records the
   wire-parity invariant.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/gitlab_sync_tools.dart` — `_listProjectJobs` emits
  `scope%5B%5D=` instead of literal `scope[]=`, with a comment explaining
  the two-transport invariant (gh-380).
- `test/js/sync_tools/gitlab_job_list_tools_test.dart` — new transport-parity
  regression test in a dedicated `testjoblisttools_p5()` group (keeps every
  group function under the 60-line `method_size` gate).

Commits on `ai/gh-380` (pushed, new head for validation):

- `d63d517c` (auto-save) — scope[] pre-encoding + regression test
- `c01b8c63` — p5 group split (method_size gate)

## Test Coverage

- New regression test exercises both transports deterministically
  (dispose→curl, await-boot→bridge) — the previously racy assertion can no
  longer flip with load.
- Full suite, CI-identical sharding (Dart 3.13.5, QuickJS built locally):
  - shard 0: **1015 passed**
  - shard 1 (the red one): **1006 passed, 12 skipped**
  - shard 2: **955 passed, 1 skipped**
  - shard 3: **948 passed, 3 skipped**
  - total **3924 passed** (PR baseline 3923 + 1 new regression test), 0 failed
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` — clean; `dart analyze` — no issues.
- `crap4dart check --all` — 19 passed / 1 failed locally where the single
  failure is `test_coverage` (no `coverage/lcov.info` exists outside CI;
  CI's `test` shards generate it and `gate` merges it — full local
  `dart test --coverage` run launched to confirm); `method_size` violation
  introduced mid-rework was fixed by the p5 split. `crap4dart analyze` —
  Max CRAP 0.00, threshold 8.00 OK.
- E2E (AC1–AC3) still requires live GitLab credentials — not runnable in
  this sandbox (unchanged from the PR's original note).
